In microservice architectures, uncoordinated scaling and sudden traffic spikes can cause severe overloads and destructive retry storms that indiscriminately reject critical, high-value transactions. To resolve these issues, researchers developed DiffTry (Differential Retries), a lightweight and stateless mechanism that transforms standard retries into a prioritization tool by assigning class-specific retry limits. Operating directly at the retry decision point without requiring cross-service coordination or explicit overload detection, DiffTry effectively shields high-priority traffic while suppressing retry amplification. The authors established an analytical network model proving that DiffTry provides formal guarantees of monotonic success-rate improvements across complex, multi-service topologies. Finally, experimental evaluations on a live Kubernetes deployment confirmed that DiffTry functions effectively as a drop-in service-mesh plugin, substantially reducing rejections for important transactions without requiring application-level code modifications.
